paper.title: A Self-Improving AI System for Cement Kiln Control in Saudi Arabia

scenario: the operator is described by class, never by name: a cement company in Saudi Arabia running several integrated plants, each with a preheater and precalciner kiln line of several thousand tonnes of clinker a day, with the first phase on one kiln line at one plant for one quarter, reading the seven systems of record through a one-way boundary and never writing to the control system
source: chapter 5 of the paper (the sixteen objects in 5.1, the status vocabularies in 5.2, the Kiln line record in 5.3), the properties and the labelled typed links of Figure 4 (its title counts eleven; nine are labelled, the recipe to fuel lot link is drawn without a label and taken from Table 8, and the eleventh is not drawn), and the anchors and links of Table 8; the Shift anchor follows Table 3 (the shift log holds actions and handovers); the upset and the three people are anchored in the model itself (5.2); properties the figure truncates are left out.

write_paths: the adapter tier (integration, telemetry and ops systems adapter families, read only against the seven systems of record through the one-way boundary, stamping every record with provenance and receipt time)
a named person confirming, rejecting or annotating a draft, written into the object model and the decision record and never into any system of record

the surfaces used by named control room operators, shift supervisors and the production manager (identity issued inside the boundary): cause confirmations, setpoint draft approvals and shift handover confirmations
human_loop: agents draft and people decide: the control room operator confirms the upset agent's cause and recovery draft, the shift supervisor approves the setpoint agent's draft, and the production manager confirms the shift agent's handover and energy and quality comparison; operators and supervisors make every setpoint change and no agent writes to the control system
